patients.summary: High school math teacher with recurrent genital HSV on episodic valacyclovir who joins the practice in 2022. Three deliveries follow in consecutive Januaries at an outside hospital: a vaginal birth with a third-degree sphincter injury (2024), a cesarean for active HSV lesions in labor (2025), and a trial of labor after cesarean ending in uterine rupture, emergency repair and transfusion (2026), after the practice last saw her.

documents.title: New patient inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 29 y/o teacher looking for a new primary care doctor; her old office is closing its adult panel. Went over membership and what insurance still covers (labs, imaging, specialists). She'd like to start. New patient physical booked for Tues 9/13 at 8:00 before school. Asked her to sign the release so we can get her old chart. BCBS PPO card info entered.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 3 days, starting at the first sign of an outbreak

social.value: Social, 1-2 glasses of wine per month

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT. 29F, teaches math at the high school, here to establish. Prior PCP office closing its adult panel; release signed, chart requested.

Concerns: none acute. Wants a doctor she can reach.

Hx: Genital herpes for years, flares a few times a year at most, usually tingling first. Keeps valacyclovir at home and takes 500 mg twice a day for 3 days when she feels it coming; that has worked well. Never on daily suppression. Last flare she thinks was spring.
OB: G1P1, one vaginal birth in 2017, no complications. No surgeries.
Meds: valacyclovir 500 mg BID x3 days PRN prodrome.
Allergies: none to medications.
FHx: mother had a C-section; one sister also has recurrent HSV-2; maternal aunt with osteoporosis. No early heart disease or cancers she knows of.
Social: married, one child at home. Never smoked. Wine once or twice a month.

ROS negative except as above.

Exam: Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No genital exam today, she has no active lesions. Skin clear. Mood and affect normal.
PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 1.

A/P
1. Preventive: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH. One-time HIV and hep C screening, she agrees. Pap/HPV per old records (believes 2021, normal); will confirm when chart arrives. Flu and COVID boosters next month when the fall supply is in.
2. Recurrent genital HSV: continue episodic valacyclovir; discussed daily suppression as an option if flares get more frequent. She prefers episodic. Message us for refills.

RTC yearly, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your results from Tuesday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Grace, everything from Tuesday came back fine: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, thyroid and cholesterol are all in the normal range, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens are negative. Nothing to do. Good to meet you.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based. Satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Prior office sent 38 pages (2014 to 2022). Summary for the chart:
- Pap with HPV co-test 08/10/2021: negative cytology, HPV not detected.
- Vaccines: HPV series x3 2007-2008; Tdap 04/2017 during pregnancy; COVID primary series 04/2021.
- Problem list there: genital herpes, recurrent, on episodic valacyclovir.
- Allergies: NKDA.
Abstracted and sent to PCP inbox. Originals scanned under Media.

documents.title: Outside records reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Old chart reviewed. Matches her history. Pap/HPV normal 2021, next due 2026. Tdap 2017. Nothing outstanding.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came in after school. Afebrile, feeling well. Screening questions negative. Flu (quadrivalent) L deltoid, Pfizer bivalent booster R deltoid. Lot numbers in the immunization record. Waited 15 min, no reaction. VIS given.

documents.title: Refill please
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning - I've got the tingling that usually means a flare is coming. I have enough valacyclovir for today and tomorrow but not the full three days. Could you send more to the pharmacy on Main? Thanks, Grace

documents.title: RE: Refill please
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sent - valacyclovir 500 mg, one twice a day for 3 days, with a few courses' worth and refills so you're not caught short next time. Start now. If it isn't settling in a week or looks different from your usual, let me know.

documents.title: Valacyclovir refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: valacyclovir 500 mg tab, 1 PO BID x 3 days at onset of outbreak. Disp #18, RF 2. E-prescribed.

orders.reason: prenatal care, intrauterine pregnancy about 5 weeks

documents.title: Positive pregnancy test
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called on her lunch break. Two positive home tests this weekend. LMP 4/10/23, cycles regular. Planned, she is happy. No bleeding or cramping. Hx genital HSV - she knows not to use the valacyclovir in pregnancy without talking to OB; reminded her to tell OB about the herpes history. Wants the same OB group as last time. Referral to OB sent. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Note to chart
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Agree. Pregnancy added to the list. OB to manage prenatal care; we'll keep seeing her for primary care. Valacyclovir on hold for now, OB to advise.

documents.title: Obstetrics: new OB visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRICS GROUP
New OB visit 06/13/2023

Re: Grace Paquette, DOB 11/02/1992

Thank you for referring Ms. Paquette, G2P1001, seen at 9w1d by LMP 04/10/2023. First-trimester ultrasound shows a single intrauterine pregnancy with cardiac activity, size consistent with dates; EDD 01/15/2024.

OB history: term spontaneous vaginal delivery 2017, uncomplicated. No prior uterine surgery.
Medical: recurrent genital HSV, episodic valacyclovir, none currently.
Allergies: NKDA.

Prenatal labs drawn: blood type and screen, CBC, rubella and varicella immunity, hepatitis B, HIV, syphilis, urine culture, all unremarkable; she is rubella immune.
Exam: BP normal, normal pelvic exam, no lesions.

Plan: routine prenatal care every 4 weeks; anatomy scan at 20 weeks. We will see her through delivery.

Obstetrics attending

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL. 30F, G2P1, 23 wks by dates, prenatal care with OB, going well; anatomy scan normal per pt. Back at school, tired by Friday but managing.
No HSV flare since last October.
Meds: valacyclovir on hold in pregnancy.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx/social unchanged.

Exam: Comfortable. Gravid abdomen, fundus near umbilicus. Heart RRR, lungs clear. No edema. Thyroid normal.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P
- Health maintenance up to date. Pap 2021, next 2026.
- CBC today since OB will want a 28-wk check anyway; she asked us to draw while here.
- Flu and COVID in October, both recommended in pregnancy. Tdap will be done by OB in the third trimester.
- HSV: per OB.
See next year.

documents.title: CBC result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood count is normal for this point in pregnancy - the hemoglobin is a touch lower than last year, which is expected as blood volume expands. I'll send a copy to your OB.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: MA
documents.body: 26 wks pregnant, feels well, no fever. Flu (preservative-free quadrivalent) and updated Pfizer COVID given, one each arm. Observed 15 min, fine. Copy of record emailed to her for OB.

documents.title: Obstetrics: prenatal update
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRICS GROUP
Prenatal visit 11/21/2023, 32w1d

Ms. Paquette continues to do well. Fundal height appropriate, fetal heart tones normal, BP normal, no edema. Glucose challenge at 27 weeks normal. Tdap given today.
Plan: visits every 2 weeks, then weekly from 36 weeks. Delivery planned at our hospital.

Obstetrics attending
